title: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have model parameter counts far exceeding dense models of equivalent compute cost, making checkpoint-based fault tolerance extremely expensive in terms of checkpoint size, write bandwidth, and recovery time for distributed training at >10k node scale.
method: MoC-System exploits the sparse activation pattern of MoE models: only a subset of experts is activated per token, so most expert parameters are not updated in any given training step. The system uses a Model-on-Checkpoint (MoC) approach that selectively checkpoints only the experts that were actually updated (activated) during a training step, avoiding checkpointing dormant expert parameters. This is combined with distributed checkpoint orchestration to overlap checkpoint I/O with forward/backward computation and expert-parallel sharding to minimize per-node checkpoint volume.

title: Symbiotic Task Scheduling and Data Prefetching
problem: Hardware task-parallel systems that operate with fine-grained tasks (approx. 100-cycle execution time) cannot benefit from conventional hardware prefetchers because tasks are too short for prefetches to complete before the task finishes, leaving DRAM latency fully exposed and undermining the performance gains of hardware task management.
method: The Task-Seeded Prefetcher (TSP) learns the data-access pattern of each task function type and issues prefetches as soon as a task descriptor is queued by the hardware task scheduler, using the descriptor as a seed to identify which memory addresses the task will access. The Memory Response Task Scheduler (MRS) augments the baseline task-to-core dispatch policy by monitoring prefetch completion status from TSP: when a task's prefetches are done, MRS preferentially dispatches it to a ready core, maximizing prefetch utilization without stalling the pipeline. Together, TSP and MRS form a symbiotic pair where scheduling drives prefetching and prefetch status informs scheduling.

title: Exploring and Mitigating Failure Behavior of Large Language Model Training Workloads in HPC Systems
problem: LLM training on HPC systems faces reliability challenges from transient faults; failure patterns are more complex than DNN inference due to massive parameter scale and iterative updates
method: LLMFI fault injection tool; 300K+ fault injection experiments (5K+ GPU node-hours); LLMFT ML-based fault tolerance framework with heuristic feature extraction, fault detector, dual recovery mechanisms

title: Anchor First, Accelerate Next: Revolutionizing GNNs with PIM by Harnessing Stationary Data
problem: Graph neural network processing on PIM architectures suffers from cross-bank data movement; only 35.6% of data stays stationary within PIM units on average, degrading efficiency as PIM density increases.
method: Anchor architecture uses hardware-software co-design. Software-level Mastav graph partitioning algorithm allocates vertices and edges to maximize stationary data within PIM banks. Hardware-level customized dataflow ensures non-stationary data is accessed and distributed exactly once. An optimized communication mechanism reduces redundant transfers through critical path analysis.

title: ACRS: Adjacent Computation Resource Sharing among Partitioned GPU Sub-Cores
problem: Modern GPU sub-core partitioning reduces power and area but prevents task distribution across sub-cores; functional units (FUs) frequently stall waiting for results while adjacent sub-cores have unoccupied FUs, wasting compute capacity.
method: ACRS framework enables dynamic sharing of functional units among adjacent sub-cores through two modules: Shared FU Issue (SF_ISSUE) monitors operand collector and FU status, offloading stalled instructions to unoccupied FUs in adjacent sub-cores; Shared FU Write Back (SF_WriteBack) routes results back. Fixed target core assignment minimizes wiring overhead.

title: FLEXPROF: Flexible, Side-Channel-Free Memory Access
problem: Secure memory controllers that prevent microarchitectural side-channels by allocating fixed 'turns' to co-scheduled VMs impose a ~2x performance slowdown because the schedule must conservatively handle worst-case mixed read/write patterns, leaving memory bus utilization inefficient.
method: FlexProf introduces two types of memory controller turns: read-optimized turns and write-optimized turns, selected via coarse-grain application profiling that observes the read/write ratio without leaking sensitive information. Each turn type is sized and structured for its dominant operation. Flexibility is added so that a read-optimized turn can opportunistically issue writes when read slots are idle (and vice versa), improving utilization while preserving the fixed-turn structure needed to prevent timing side-channels between VMs.

title: 8.5 A Command-Aware Hybrid LDO for Advanced HBM Interfaces with 150μA Quiescent Current and 20pF On-Chip Capacitor Achieving Sub-10mV Voltage Droop in 400ps Settling Time
problem: HBM3E/HBM4 interfaces suffer from power-supply-induced jitter (PSIJ) caused by sudden load current surges in write-data-strobe (WDQS) buffers, leading to voltage droop and sampling errors in high-bandwidth memory.
method: A command-aware hybrid LDO uses predictive techniques triggered by command signals (ACT_CMD) to mitigate voltage droop before WDQS buffer transients occur, achieving sub-10mV droop with minimal on-chip capacitance (20pF) and low quiescent current (150μA).

title: YAP: Yield Modeling and Simulation for Advanced Packaging
problem: Cu-Cu hybrid bonding for chiplet integration suffers from yield loss due to overlay errors, particle defects, Cu recess variations, wafer roughness, and Cu density; no efficient analytical model for rapid design optimization.
method: YAP: analytical yield model for W2W and D2W Cu-Cu hybrid bonding accounting for five key failure mechanisms; near-analytical model compared against Monte Carlo simulation; 10,000x faster runtime.

title: An Efficient Compute-in-Memory based Accelerator for Point-based Point Cloud Neural Networks
problem: Point-based point cloud neural networks are computationally intensive and exhibit poor performance on resource-constrained edge devices due to irregular data access patterns and high memory bandwidth requirements.
method: Point-CIM proposes a reconfigurable CIM unit exploiting zero-bit-skipping sparsity, Voxel-Morton-sorted Partitioning (VMP) with Channel-wise Minimum base point selection for improved decomposition sparsity, and Bit-level Truncation Quantization (BTQ) for bit-width compression without extra hardware. Pre-decomposition data movement strategy reduces transfers between buffer and CIM array.

title: Towards Supporting QIR: Steps for Adopting the Quantum Intermediate Representation
problem: Quantum computing intermediate representations (IRs) are critical for optimization, but adoption pathways are unclear; converting existing simulators to support QIR requires significant effort.
method: Demonstration: convert quantum circuit simulator to QIR runtime. Outline multiple adoption approaches. Benchmark performance vs original simulator. Show classical control flow support.

title: TianheEngine: Hierarchy-aware Adaptive Partitioning System for Trillion-scale Graph Processing
problem: Traditional graph partitioning strategies neglect hierarchical communication variances in modern HPC systems, causing prohibitive cross-layer communication overhead when processing trillion-scale graphs across thousands of nodes.
method: TianheEngine: hierarchy-aware adaptive partitioning system that exploits communication hierarchy and graph sparsity characteristics to improve communication efficiency in distributed graph processing.

title: 35.8 DustNet: A Network of Time-Division Multiplexed Ultrasonic Implants with 16-Level ASK Backscatter Modulation
problem: Multi-implant wireless neural recording networks require simultaneous data rates of 200-400kb/s from 4-8 distributed implants at depths of several cm with minimal infection risk, exceeding capabilities of existing RF/optical approaches.
method: DustNet uses time-division multiplexing of ultrasonic implants with 16-level ASK backscatter modulation to achieve 50kb/s per implant. Ultrasound carrier frequencies in the single-digit MHz range minimize tissue absorption, enabling multi-cm implant depth while maximizing channel bandwidth efficiency.

title: STREAMINGGS: Voxel-Based Streaming 3D Gaussian Splatting with Memory Optimization and Architectural Support
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) struggles to achieve real-time 90 FPS rendering on mobile devices (currently only 2-9 FPS), with existing accelerators optimizing compute efficiency but ignoring memory efficiency, resulting in redundant DRAM traffic.
method: STREAMINGGS implements fully streaming algorithm-architecture co-design with fine-grained pipelining and transforms from tile-centric rendering (tile-first, load all Gaussians) to memory-centric rendering (stream Gaussian groups, load only touched tiles). This approach reduces DRAM traffic and enables better prefetching and memory utilization on mobile GPUs.

title: Hierarchical Prefetching: A Software-Hardware Instruction Prefetcher for Server Applications
problem: Server-side applications have large instruction working sets that cause severe front-end bottlenecks even with state-of-the-art fetch-directed instruction prefetching (FDIP), because record-and-replay prefetchers lose coverage and timeliness when actual control flow diverges from predicted control flow.
method: Hierarchical Prefetching identifies coarse-grained functionality blocks called Bundles—spanning tens to hundreds of kilobytes of code—through lightweight static software analysis of the server binary. Hardware then uses a compact record-and-replay mechanism (under 2KB of on-chip SRAM) that prefetches entire Bundles when a bundle entry point is detected, rather than individual cache lines. Most Bundle metadata is stored in main memory, keeping on-chip storage minimal. The bundle formation analysis groups functionally related code regions that tend to execute together, tolerating control flow variability by prefetching the entire functional region rather than a precise sequence.

title: UniCoS: A Unified Neural and Accelerator Co-Search Framework for CNNs and ViTs
problem: Current algorithm-hardware co-search methods suffer from lengthy training times and inadequate exploration of hardware design spaces, resulting in suboptimal joint architecture-accelerator solutions.
method: UniCoS introduces a training-free accuracy proxy that evaluates network accuracy in seconds and a clustering-based algorithm for exploring heterogeneous dataflows, enabling rapid joint exploration of both CNN and ViT network architectures and accelerator designs.

title: DejaVuzz: Disclosing Transient Execution Bugs with Dynamic Swappable Memory and Differential Information Flow Tracking Assisted Processor Fuzzing
problem: Existing hardware fuzzers for detecting transient execution vulnerabilities (e.g., Spectre, Meltdown variants) suffer from poor microarchitectural controllability and observability: they cannot reliably set up the precise microarchitectural state needed to trigger transient execution paths, nor detect covert information leakage resulting from such paths.
method: DejaVuzz introduces two synergistic mechanisms: Dynamic Swappable Memory (DSM), which swaps physical memory pages at runtime to precisely control the microarchitectural state of TLBs, caches, and branch predictors needed to trigger transient execution; and Differential Information Flow Tracking (DIFT), which instruments the processor simulator to observe whether secret data leaks through transient microarchitectural side channels. The fuzzer generates test programs that exercise transient execution windows by leveraging DSM to reset microarchitectural state between tests, and uses DIFT differential analysis to detect when information from a secret source reaches an observable side channel (e.g., cache timing). This enables both high coverage and precise detection of leakage.
